title: astra.registry.decision/1
description:
log/decisions/<YYYY>/<MM>/<decision_id>.json — the public decision log (contract DEC-7; B.4). One file per bot decision about a submission or a fingerprint, plus one author-action file per version an `A_YANK` names. bot/lib/decisions.mjs is the only writer (BOT-34); it stamps `schema` and derives `decision_id` (BOT-35), and refuses a caller that supplies either.

EXACTLY DEC-7'S TWENTY-FIVE MEMBERS. DEC-7's own sentence is "with only these members, absent where they do not apply", so `additionalProperties` is false and `$comment` is NOT among them. This record crosses a party boundary — the plugins service, the panel and a guest all read it (SCOPE-3) — and a member one party admits and another refuses is a two-way-test failure (§0.8) found in production by whichever side guessed wrong. `issue` is the mutation registry plan B-T2.1's canary list names: it is a member of the queue entry and of nothing else, and a composer that copied one would put an issue number into the public log after OD-2 ended the issue channel.

SIX ARE REQUIRED, AND THE REST ARE "ABSENT WHERE THEY DO NOT APPLY". A record with no `decided_at`, `actor`, `trigger` or `state` is not a decision that lacked detail; it is a file that does not say what was decided, when, by whom, or under what. DEC-7's own example of legitimate absence — `fingerprint`, `plugin_id` and `version` for an `A_WITHDRAW` from `received` — touches none of the six. `schema` and `decision_id` are required because the writer stamps them and a reader outside this repository finds the record by its path and identifies it by its `schema`.

ABSENT MEANS ABSENT, NOT NULL. No member here admits null. "Absent where they do not apply" is DEC-7's phrase and a null is a value: a record carrying `"commit": null` states that the release commit is the null one, which is a different claim from not making one, and the two are indistinguishable to a reader that tests for presence. bot/baseline.mjs already meets this — the one published version with no release commit is carried by OMITTING the member and is named in the commit message.

`repository_id` AND `repository_owner_id` ARE STRINGS. §0.7: canonical base-10 digit strings, never coerced. See schema/identity-v1.json for the failure in full; the short form is that JSON's one number type is a double and 9007199254740993 round-trips as …92.

`reasons` IS AN ARRAY OF B.7 CODE STRINGS, NEVER OBJECTS (contract 0.12.0's m4). The `items` rule here refuses an object by type and free text by pattern, which is DEC-7's "Never: … free text" made mechanical. It deliberately does NOT enumerate the codes: the closed list lives in bot/lib/codes.mjs and in FLOW-13's table, a schema that copied it would be a second copy that goes stale silently, and a decision record carrying a code this registry has retired is still a true record of what was decided that day. What this pattern buys is the thing a stale enum could not: prose never reaches the public log.

THE TWO SHAPES, AND WHY ONE OF THEM IS NOT EXPRESSED HERE. Since contract 0.13.0 (n5) DEC-7 describes two records: the submission record, and the AUTHOR-ACTION record an `A_YANK` compiles to, which carries exactly thirteen members — `schema`, `decision_id`, `decided_at`, `actor` `author`, `trigger` `moderation`, `plugin_id`, `version`, `repo`, `repository_id`, `repository_owner_id`, `state` `yanked`, `reasons` `["A_YANK"]`, `category` `author_request` — and NO `submission_id` and NO `fingerprint`, which a yank has not. Every one of those thirteen is a member of the set below, so a valid author-action record validates here; what this file cannot say is the conditional "when the record is an author action, these two members are forbidden". tools/lib/jsonschema.mjs implements no `if`/`then` and refuses an unknown keyword outright rather than ignoring it, so the rule sits in tools/validate.mjs beside the queue entry's, and bot/lib/decisions.mjs refuses it a second time at composition. Detector B row 2 on the service's side matches an author-action record BY its having no `submission_id`, so a record that carried one would be classified over there as something else entirely.

THE OTHER RULE tools/validate.mjs CARRIES, WHICH NO PER-RECORD SCHEMA CAN. BOT-34's second Check clause counts: a commit whose changed listings show n versions moved to `yanked` under an `A_YANK` must carry n author-action records, one per version, and is refused otherwise. It is a statement about a SET of files, and every file in that set can be individually valid while the set is wrong — which is exactly the failure it exists to catch, since an `A_YANK` names versions plural while DEC-7's `version` is a single member.

WHAT NOTHING HERE CAN CHECK. That `decision_id` is in fact the first 32 hex of SHA-256 over BOT-35's domain-separated key is a statement about a derivation, not about this file: the pattern below admits any 32 lowercase hex, and two composers producing two different ids for one tuple both pass it. bot/lib/decisions.mjs is where that is one function, and bot/tests/decisions.test.mjs is where the same tuple is asserted to give the same id twice. Likewise the path: that this record sits under its own `decided_at`'s year and month is `recordPath`'s to enforce. Recorded as gaps rather than implied by this file's existence.

decision_id.$comment: §0.7: 32 lowercase hex, the first 32 of SHA-256 over BOT-35's domain-separated key. The derivation is bot/lib/decisions.mjs's; this only says what a derived id looks like.

submission_id.$comment: §0.7's lowercase UUID v4 or v7. PRIV-2 exempts it by member name. Absent on an author-action record, which a yank gives no submission — enforced in tools/validate.mjs, which is where the conditional lives.

decided_at.$comment: §0.7: RFC 3339 UTC, whole seconds, `Z`. The pattern cannot say the date is real (`2026-02-31T00:00:00Z` matches it); tools/validate.mjs round-trips it through Date, which is the other half.

actor.$comment: DEC-7's closed list, as schema/contract-tokens-v1.json publishes it under `decision-record actors`. PRIV-10 makes every historic approver `system`.

moderator.$comment: A handle, and THE ONLY MEMBER HERE THAT MAY CARRY ONE. PRIV-2 permits it in this member and in no other; tools/priv-scan.mjs's `handleOk` for this document names `moderator` alone. A handle anywhere else is a moderator's name in a place nobody will think to look for one.

trigger.$comment: DEC-7's closed list, as the token file publishes it under `decision-record triggers`. `ci` needs ID-72's precondition; `issue`, `ping`, `dispatch` and `legacy` end at R6 (registry plan ROLL-22), and the token file is where that `until <step>` is recorded — not here, because a record written before R6 stays true after it.

version.$comment: A SINGLE semver, and that is load-bearing: an `A_YANK` names versions plural, so a yank of three versions is three records, not one record with a joined `version`. tools/lib/semver.mjs's SEMVER_PATTERN.

repo.$comment: `owner/name`. PRIV-2 permits a repository coordinate; the owner half is a login and is permitted only here and in `tag`, which is why tools/priv-scan.mjs takes both out before applying the subject-id shape.

tag.$comment: tools/lib/tags.mjs's TAG_PATTERN, the one spelling of a release tag in this repository.

commit.$comment: The attested release commit, 40 lowercase hex. OMITTED, never null, when the release has none: one published version in this registry predates release.commit being bound at approval, and bot/baseline.mjs carries it by omission and names it in the run log.

artifact_digests.$comment: `<platform>:<sha256>`, the form bot/lib/policy/release.mjs builds and bot/baseline.mjs checks, sorted and without repeats. A digest with no sha256 behind it is not a digest.

fingerprint.$comment: bot/lib/policy/release.mjs's FINGERPRINT_CHARS: 16 lowercase hex over six facts about one submission. Absent on an author-action record — a yank hashes no release — which tools/validate.mjs enforces.

state.$comment: DEFINED BY A SHAPE RATHER THAN BY A LIST, AND DELIBERATELY. The contract fixes closed lists for a SUBMISSION's states (B.3) and for a version's (`yanked`), and DEC-7 covers decisions about both, and about a fingerprint besides; it names no single list of its own. Enumerating the union here would be this file inventing a closed list the contract does not have, and the first legitimate eleventh value would be refused by a schema nobody could point at a requirement for. The shape refuses free text, which is what DEC-7 forbids.

reasons.$comment: An array of B.7 code strings (m4). An object fails on type; prose fails on pattern. An empty array is refused because DEC-7's answer to "no reasons apply" is that the member is absent.

category.$comment: §7.2's categories, as the token file publishes them under `moderation categories`. FLOW-79's author yank carries `author_request`.

appeal_of.$comment: The `service_decision_id` or the `decision_id` appealed (MOD-33, and bot/moderation/README.md's table), so either §0.7's UUID or 32 lowercase hex.

outcome.$comment: DEC-7's closed pair, as the token file publishes it under `appeal outcome`.

declared_interest.$comment: A FLAG, never a name (MOD-12): true when a moderator declared a conflict. A string here would be the one place a conflict could be described in free text, in the public log, for ever.

publish_after.$comment: §0.7: RFC 3339 UTC, whole seconds, `Z`. The same moment the queue entry carries (BOT-33; B.4).

run.$comment: §0.7's `run_id`, or `run_id/run_attempt` — the same grammar BOT-37's `Run:` trailer takes, and for the same reason: correlation must outlive a 14-day artifact, and a bare id is the only form of it that cannot carry a login. NOT the run URL, whose owner segment is one.
